items.prompt: Explain why groundwater is important for farming and settlement in the interior of Namibia.
items.canonical_answer: Most interior channels are ephemeral and flow briefly after rain. High evaporation removes much water from open reservoirs. Boreholes and wells can tap water stored underground, protected from direct open-water evaporation. Where aquifer storage, recharge, quality and abstraction permit, this sustains farms and settlements through dry periods; boreholes can still fail or be depleted.
marking_guidance: 1 mark for the cause: mainly ephemeral interior channels; 1 for the link to high evaporation from open stores; 1 for the link to protected underground storage tapped by boreholes; 1 for the effect of dry-period supply, conditional on adequate usable groundwater.

items.prompt: Explain how repeated low inflows can create a supply problem even if the first dry season is buffered by a reservoir.

items.prompt: On a contour sketch, a river flows from north to south and a dam wall crosses it; the planned water level is the 255 m contour. A learner shades the reservoir south of the wall. Explain the error and the test that locates the reservoir correctly.
items.canonical_answer: The confusion places stored water downstream. Water approaching from the north is held back, so the correct reservoir lies north of the wall, filling the upstream valley up to the 255 m contour. The test is to follow the flow towards the wall and shade only the upstream valley below the stated water level.
marking_guidance: 1 mark for identifying the confusion of upstream with downstream; 1 for the correct distinction and discriminating test: shade the upstream (northern) valley up to the 255 m contour.

items.prompt:
A hypothetical reservoir starts an interval with 100 water units, receives twenty, supplies thirty to users and loses ten to evaporation. Other changes are absent; no rainfall baseline is given.
(a) Name the loss process changing liquid water into atmospheric vapour. [1]
(b) Calculate closing storage. [2]
(c) Describe three features of the stock/flow account. [3]
(d) What judgement is supported about the claim “this interval alone proves meteorological drought”? [1]
items.canonical_answer: (a) Evaporation. (b) 100+20−30−10 = 80 units. (c) Inflow is twenty; combined outflow is forty, twice inflow; stock falls twenty units or 20% of its opening value. Credit three distinct relevant observations, without treating equivalent expressions of the same decline as separate points. (d) Drought is not established without the relevant rainfall baseline and sustained-period evidence.
marking_guidance: (a) 1 A mark for evaporation.
(b) 2 B marks for the full stock-plus-inflow-minus-losses method and correct closing value/unit.
(c) 3 B marks for distinct input, output and stock-change patterns supported by the resource data.
(d) 1 C mark for the supported judgement distinguishing a water balance from a meteorological diagnosis.

items.prompt: How far do you agree that Windhoek's water supply was secure at the time of the city's August 2025 announcement? Use its sources and the dated conditions in your answer. [5]
items.canonical_answer: Partly agree for that short-term position. Windhoek uses the Von Bach, Swakoppoort and Omatako dams, boreholes and reclaimed water from Goreangab. Following the 2024/25 rains, the city reported in August 2025 reserves for at least two rainy seasons, lifted restrictions and began aquifer recharge. Against this, evaporation, recurring drought and growing demand remain, and there is no local perennial river. The announcement supported improved short-term security with continued management; it cannot establish conditions in a later year.
marking_guidance: Up to 4 C marks for a developed reason on each side, weighing diverse sources and the dated August 2025 reserves against evaporation, drought and rising demand.
1 C mark for a supported, time-bounded decision; do not require a claim about current restrictions.
